stories.headline: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, tops AA Index v5, but limits access to cyber defenders

key_facts.fact: On October 28, 2026, Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, which it calls its strongest model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities, two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're announcing the next frontier model: Gemini 4 Carbon, our strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long horizon capabilities... Building on Gemini 4 Argon, which was launched two weeks ago

key_facts.fact: Carbon scores 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro (finding vulnerabilities), 54.8% on ExploitGym (exploitation) and 71.0% on CWE-bench (patching), and Google says it generates secure code at more than 2x Argon's success rate.
key_facts.excerpt: landing a firm lead in SEC-bench Pro (88.2%) for finding vulnerabilities, ExploitGym (54.8%) for exploitation, and CWE-bench (71.0%) for patching... Carbon achieves more than 2x uplift in success rate for generating secure code over Argon

key_facts.fact: Artificial Analysis ranks Carbon (high) first on its Intelligence Index v5 at 59, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 58, GPT-6 Astra at 57 and Argon at 50.
key_facts.excerpt: Independent evaluator Artificial Analysis places Carbon, using high reasoning, first on its Intelligence Index v5.0 with 59 points, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 58, GPT-6 Astra at 57 and Argon at 50.

key_facts.fact: On Artificial Analysis' Coding Agent Index, Carbon scores 59, three points behind Claude Code with Opus 5.5 (62), and costs $7.76 per Intelligence Index task, about 23% less than Opus 5.5 ($10.04); its hallucination rate rose from 4% (Argon) to 11%.
key_facts.excerpt: With Antigravity CLI, Gemini 4 Carbon (high) scores 59 only 3 points behind Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 (max, 62)... Gemini 4 Carbon costs $7.76 per Intelligence Index task, ~23% less than Claude Opus 5.5 (max, $10.04)... its hallucination rate rises from 4% to 11%

key_facts.fact: Access starts with a subset of cyber defenders via Google's Fairwind Program; Google says it is taking part in the US government's voluntary pre-release testing process and will expand to developers and consumers after iterating on guardrails.
key_facts.excerpt: actively engaged in the U.S. government's voluntary process for pre-release model testing. Starting this week, we will make Carbon available to a subset of cyber defenders and will gradually phase access to additional trusted partners through our Fairwind Program.

key_facts.fact: Introductory pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, matching Argon, rising to $4/$20 after the introductory period, for which Google has not set an end date.
key_facts.excerpt: Google says Carbon will launch at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens... a footnote specifies subsequent prices of $4 and $20... Google hasn't specified in its release blog post when Carbon's introductory period will end.

stories.headline: GitHub makes Copilot Fusion multi-model router generally available at Universe 2026

key_facts.fact: On October 28, 2026, at GitHub Universe, GitHub made Copilot Fusion generally available; instead of picking a model, users pick Fusion and it routes and orchestrates which models handle each task.
key_facts.excerpt: GitHub Copilot Fusion is generally available. Instead of picking a model for each task, choose Copilot Fusion and let Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate which models it uses for you.

key_facts.fact: On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Copilot Fusion Max scored 60, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max, at about half the API cost per task, half the tokens and about 40% less time per task.
key_facts.excerpt: In the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Copilot Fusion Max scored 60, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max. It delivered that result at about half the average API cost per task, using about half as many tokens and taking about 40% less time per task.

key_facts.fact: Fusion uses three workflows: a single model, a cascade (cheap model drafts, a quality check escalates to a stronger model), and critique (one model drafts, another reviews); users are billed for each model used at standard rates, with a temporary 30% discount on paid plans.
key_facts.excerpt: Cascade: An efficient model drafts a response. A quality check determines whether to accept it or escalate to a stronger model. Critique: One model drafts an initial response, another model reviews it... For a limited time, users on paid Copilot plans will receive a 30% discount

key_facts.fact: GitHub also said Enterprise customers can now use all Copilot features without a separate Copilot subscription, paying for the AI credits they use.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting today, GitHub Enterprise customers can use all Copilot features without buying a separate subscription. That includes GitHub Copilot app, code review, automations, and more. You pay for the AI credits you use.

key_facts.fact: Satya Nadella said Copilot Fusion delivers frontier-level quality at up to 77% lower cost.
key_facts.excerpt: Great momentum with GitHub Copilot too, including Copilot Fusion, announced just this morning, which delivers frontier level quality, at up to 77% lower cost.

stories.headline: Report: DeepSeek and Moonshot distilled OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on Wednesday, October 28, that DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models, citing people with direct knowledge.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese AI developers DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's powerful GPT-6 Astra model to train their latest models, The Information reported on Wednesday

key_facts.fact: The models named are Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro, released last week, and DeepSeek's V4.1-Flash 1017, launched October 17.
key_facts.excerpt: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro model, which was released last week, and DeepSeek's upgraded V4.1-Flash 1017 model, which was launched on October 17, benefited from distilling Astra

key_facts.fact: Sources said Chinese labs had focused on Anthropic's Claude until recently but shifted to Astra after Anthropic's countermeasures, which Anthropic said cut data harvested in distillation attacks by 90% to 99%.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese labs had until recently focused on Anthropic's Claude, but sources said they shifted to OpenAI after Anthropic took strong countermeasures. Anthropic said this month its new safeguards left distillers with 90% to 99% less data to harvest.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI said on September 30 that people linked to Moonshot ran a coordinated distillation campaign in July involving more than 15,000 users, which it shut down by July 28.
key_facts.excerpt: On 30 September, the company said people linked to the Kimi developer had run a coordinated campaign in July to extract the hidden reasoning behind its models' answers. OpenAI said it detected related activity involving more than 15,000 users. It shut down the campaign by 28 July

key_facts.fact: OpenAI, DeepSeek and Moonshot did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment; the report has not been independently verified.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI, DeepSeek and Moonshot AI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment

stories.headline: NYT: US officials say Megaspeed exec close to Jensen Huang is a Chinese intelligence asset

key_facts.fact: US officials concluded that Alice Huang (Huang Le), a top executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, was a Chinese intelligence asset who developed a close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the New York Times reported on October 29.
key_facts.excerpt: A top executive at a Singapore-based data center company was under scrutiny for possibly steering advanced Nvidia A.I. chips to China. And now American officials had concluded that she was a Chinese intelligence asset... she had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang

key_facts.fact: President Trump was briefed on the findings and took no action; per the Times he was concerned about disrupting Nvidia's sales and relations with China.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump was briefed on the findings about a year ago but chose not to act... Trump was concerned about disrupting Nvidia's sales and complicating relations with China.

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed's Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion in advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, and the Commerce Department's investigation was transferred to the Justice Department this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Megaspeed's Malaysian sister company bought at least $4.8 billion in advanced artificial-intelligence equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026... The Times said the Commerce Department's investigation was transferred to the Justice Department this year.

key_facts.fact: Officials do not believe Jensen Huang knew of the alleged activities, and he has not received a defensive briefing; surveillance of Alice Huang continues.
key_facts.excerpt: Mr. Huang hasn't yet been given a defensive briefing... even though the surveillance against Alice Huang continues... U.S. officials do not believe that he is aware of Ms. Huang's intelligence activities.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were 'not unusual or unexpected' and that regional cloud customers receive 'zero information relevant to national security'; the Chinese embassy called the allegations 'groundless smears'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected... Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security."... The Chinese embassy in Washington denied the allegations, saying that it was merely "groundless smears and slanders"

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed said it takes the allegations seriously and has retained outside lawyers for an internal investigation; Nvidia says it has found no evidence of smuggling.
key_facts.excerpt: Megaspeed said it took the allegations seriously and had retained outside lawyers to conduct an internal investigation... Nvidia says it complies with applicable laws and has found no evidence of smuggling.

stories.headline: Fed holds rates at 3.75%-4% as two officials vote for a hike; Warsh adds strategy-only meetings

key_facts.fact: On October 28, 2026 the FOMC voted 10-2 to keep the federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4%.
key_facts.excerpt: The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10 – 2 vote: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-3/4 to 4 percent

key_facts.fact: Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented, preferring a quarter-point rate increase.
key_facts.excerpt: Voting against the monetary policy action were Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

key_facts.fact: The statement said inflation 'remains elevated' and that 'the accumulation of more information' will guide policy; the range has been in place since a quarter-point increase in September.
key_facts.excerpt: kept the overnight funds rate in a range between 3.75%-4%, where it has been since the central bank approved a quarter percentage point increase in September. "Inflation remains elevated," the post-meeting statement said.

key_facts.fact: Chair Kevin Warsh said one FOMC meeting in 2027 will focus exclusively on monetary policy strategy, with no rate vote or statement, and two such meetings are expected in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: in 2027, one meeting will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy, with neither a vote on the federal funds rate nor a policy statement anticipated... in 2028, we'll have two meetings dedicated to discussions of strategy, and six for setting policy.

key_facts.fact: Warsh said first-half GDP growth was revised up to 2.4% from 1.8% and that third-quarter growth was likely running above 3%, with business investment rising at about a double-digit pace.
key_facts.excerpt: The GDP increase in the first half of this year was revised up from an earlier estimate of 1.8 percent up to 2.4 percent. And the third quarter appears to have brought an even more rapid advance... likely running above 3 percent growth, and business investment, likely rising at about a double-digit pace.

key_facts.fact: Reuters said the Fed upgraded its assessment of the economy and hinted further rate hikes may come depending on inflation.

stories.headline: DoorDash agrees to buy Instacart for about $17 billion, $65 a share

key_facts.fact: DoorDash and Instacart (Maplebear) announced on October 29, 2026 a definitive agreement for DoorDash to acquire Instacart at $65.00 per share, an equity value of about $17 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: today announced a definitive agreement under which DoorDash will acquire Instacart for a total value of $65.00 for each Instacart share, or an equity value of approximately $17 billion.

key_facts.fact: The price is a 26% premium to Instacart's October 22 close, the last trading day before media reports of a deal, and about 11% over Wednesday's close.
key_facts.excerpt: Instacart shareholders would receive $65 per share, mostly in cash, 11 percent over the company's closing price on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: Consideration will be at least 75% cash, funded with cash on hand and debt, backed by a 364-day bridge loan commitment from JPMorgan Chase.
key_facts.excerpt: The aggregate transaction consideration will be at least 75% cash... DoorDash has entered into a financing commitment letter with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. providing for a 364-day senior unsecured bridge loan facility

key_facts.fact: The deal is expected to close at the end of 2027 or in the first half of 2028, subject to US antitrust review and approvals in Canada and Israel; holders of about 19% of Instacart shares agreed to vote in favor.
key_facts.excerpt: expected to close in the end of 2027 or the first half of 2028, subject to approval by Instacart stockholders, the expiration or termination of the waiting period under the Hart-Scott-Rodino... including in Canada and Israel... Stockholders holding about 19% of Instacart's outstanding shares have agreed to vote in favor

key_facts.fact: DoorDash said the Instacart brand and app will remain, and Instacart customers will gain access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash.
key_facts.excerpt: DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain... Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash

key_facts.fact: DoorDash announced the deal alongside its third-quarter results.
key_facts.excerpt: DoorDash will pay $65 a share in cash and stock, it said in a statement Thursday, when it also released its third-quarter financial results.

stories.headline: Hacktivists leak data on 41,000+ DHS staff, including undercover ICE agents

key_facts.fact: Distributed Denial of Secrets published 'Icepick' on Wednesday (Oct. 28), a database identifying more than 41,000 DHS employees and contractors, obtained by a hacktivist group calling itself the Department of Peace.
key_facts.excerpt: An internal database identifying more than 41,000 employees for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS)... The data was obtained by a hacktivist group known as the Department of Peace

key_facts.fact: DDoSecrets says the data came from an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS; Okta said it has no evidence its systems were compromised.
key_facts.excerpt: DDoSecrets says the data is from DHS's Okta login system... "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our data or systems were compromised," the spokesperson says.

key_facts.fact: CBP staff account for more than half of the records and ICE for about 10,000; the files cover about a seventh of DHS's workforce, per WIRED's analysis.
key_facts.excerpt: CBP staffers account for more than half of the records. ICE accounts for about 10,000... Altogether, the files cover about a seventh of DHS's workforce

key_facts.fact: The records include groups tied to certified undercover operations, wiretap programs and tools such as Palantir's Falcon platform.
key_facts.excerpt: 39 employees across more than a dozen field offices belong to groups whose names include "CUC," which government court filings say stands for "certified undercover operation."... These include Palantir's Falcon investigative platform

key_facts.fact: DHS told the Washington Post it was 'aware of a potential breach' and working to address it.
key_facts.excerpt: The agency told the Washington Post that it was "aware of a potential breach" and was "working to address the situation swiftly and effectively."

key_facts.fact: The hackers said the leak responded to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin's July 17 pledge to 'turn up the heat' on ICE operations.
key_facts.excerpt: "On July 17th, Markwayne Mullin said he was 'turning up the heat.' This is what happens to ICE when you do that," said a spokesperson for the Department of Peace.

stories.headline: Pentagon treats freezer failures at six-plus US base stores as suspected cyberattack

key_facts.fact: Four officials told Reuters on Oct. 29 that the Pentagon is treating the late-August freezer malfunctions at US military bases as a suspected hack, reported for the first time.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon is treating the spate of mysterious freezer malfunctions that spoiled food at military bases across the United States in August as a suspected hack, according to four officials... is being reported here for the first time.

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon said a Cyber Command unit is 'working in close coordination with interagency and law enforcement partners'; Army CID's Cyber Field Office is working with French law enforcement.
key_facts.excerpt: a unit of Cyber Command — the military's cyber force — was "working in close coordination with interagency and law enforcement partners."... working with French law enforcement to better understand "the refrigeration outages in Europe."

key_facts.fact: At least six commissaries were affected, including Fort Huachuca in Arizona, where cooling units' temperatures were cranked up overnight.
key_facts.excerpt: The late August malfunctions in the United States affected at least six commissaries... In at least one of the cases, the freezers did not simply stop working; the cooling units' temperatures were cranked up overnight

key_facts.fact: A similar October attack in France overrode temperature controls at more than 350 establishments, with some units catching fire.
key_facts.excerpt: The French freezer cyberattack overrode the temperature controls on commercial cooling units in more than 350 establishments... Some French refrigeration units had the temperature turned up so high they caught fire.

key_facts.fact: Many French stores used Danfoss control boxes; records for at least one US commissary, at Naval Air Facility El Centro, list a Danfoss control system.
key_facts.excerpt: Many of the French stores used control boxes made by Danish refrigeration company Danfoss... records for at least one shop, at Naval Air Facility El Centro in California, list a Danfoss control system.

key_facts.fact: Affected bases included F.E. Warren Air Force Base in Wyoming, home to Minuteman III nuclear missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: Those affected were the FE Warren Air Force Base in Wyoming, home to the 90th Missile Wing's Minuteman III nuclear missiles; Fort Huachuca in Arizona
